subject: history

moments.title: People's Republic proclaimed
moments.body: 1 October 1949: Mao stands above Tiananmen and proclaims the People's Republic of China. The Communists have defeated Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists (Kuomintang) in a civil war resumed after WWII. Chiang retreats to Taiwan with the gold reserves.

quote.text: The Chinese people have stood up.

moments.takeaway: Mao's victory ended a century of foreign domination and civil war. The Korean War (1950-53) immediately tested the new state against the US.

moments.title: Great Leap Forward
moments.body: Forced collectivisation, backyard steel furnaces, agricultural targets divorced from reality. The result: the deadliest famine in human history. Estimates: 15-55 million deaths, with Frank Dikötter's research suggesting around 45 million.
moments.takeaway: Mao stepped back from day-to-day leadership after the disaster. Liu Shaoqi and Deng Xiaoping ran economic recovery in the early 1960s.

moments.title: Cultural Revolution
moments.who: Mao, Red Guards, the Gang of Four
moments.body: Mao launches the Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution to reassert ideological control. Schools and universities closed. Red Guards attack 'capitalist roaders' and the 'Four Olds'. Hundreds of thousands killed; millions persecuted; cultural heritage destroyed. Deng purged twice. Mao dies September 1976; the Gang of Four arrested.
moments.takeaway: Deng returned to power and from 1978 launched the 'reform and opening' — abandoning Maoist economics while keeping party rule.

now.title: Xi's China
now.body: Four decades of growth lifted around 800 million out of poverty. The 1989 Tiananmen protests were crushed (4 June). Xi Jinping (since 2012) has consolidated personal power and removed presidential term limits (2018). The CCP's centenary (2021) and the centenary of the PRC (2049) frame current policy. Sino-American rivalry now structures global politics.
now.open_questions: Can the CCP retain power through economic slowdown? Property crisis, demographic decline (population fell from 2022) and ideological tightening have created new uncertainty about the post-Deng model.

reflection: Mao's China is now mostly Deng's China — but with Xi's reassertion of party control. The Communist Party has survived because it has changed almost everything except its monopoly on power. How long that combination holds is one of the defining questions of the 21st century.
